figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Exploration of Arg-Nω-prenyltransferases. (a) Structures of the Nω-prenylguanidine-containing cyanobactins. Prenyl groups are colored
red. (b) Phylogenetic tree of representative cyanobactin prenyltransferases. The clades containing AutF and AgcF are highlighted in red. An
extended version of the tree is shown in Figure S1. (c) In vitro enzymatic reaction of DciF. The reaction was quenched at each time point and
analyzed by LC-MS with condition 1 in Table S5. The inset shows a 10-fold magnification of the extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) ion intensity
at m/z 1375.7 for the region outlined by the black box.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Structural analysis of DciF. (a) Overall structure of the apo
DciF. (b) Model of the quaternary complex of DciF/monoprenyl
Arg/DMAPP/Mg2+. The three key residues E49, H167, and T134 are
shown as sticks. Hydrogen bond interactions are represented by
yellow dashed lines. (c) In vitro enzymatic reactions of DciF mutants
E49A, T134A, and H167A.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. A key active site pocket dictates the number of prenylation rounds. (a) Model of the quaternary complex of DciF/monoprenyl Arg/
DMAPP/Mg2+. The figure was generated from the identical model shown in Figure 2b, but the view is oriented toward the prenyl group of the
ligand. (b) AlphaFold model of AutF. (c) In vitro enzymatic reaction of DciF(G65L). (d) In vitro enzymatic reaction of AutF(D65G).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Preference toward the residues flanking Arg. (a) Conversions were for the XRY library. (b) Conversions were for the LRX library.
Chromatograms and MS spectra are shown in Figures S12−S15.
